title: How Big Is a Cell, Really?
subject: biology

payoff_image.image: a single hair against warm light with a faint glowing universe of cells beneath it

beats.narration: Think your world is small? An invisible universe is hiding under one 80-micrometer strand of your hair.
beats.claim: a human hair is about 80 micrometers wide and hides a microscopic universe
beats.visual_question: what hides under a single strand of hair?
beats.visual_answer: a full-bleed hair shaft crossing the frame with a hidden microscopic world at its edge

beats.narration: Your eyes bottom out near one tenth of a millimeter. Anything smaller stays a rumor you can only measure.
beats.claim: the naked eye resolves detail only down to about 0.1 millimeters
beats.visual_question: where does human vision hit its floor?
beats.visual_answer: macro close-up of the hair edge dissolving past the eye's resolution limit, measurement ticks fading

beats.narration: So dive: through the skin, into a cell 30 micrometers wide, a mitochondrion 30 times smaller, then DNA just 2 nanometers thin.
beats.claim: one continuous dive runs from hair width through a cell and a mitochondrion down to DNA at 2 nanometers
beats.visual_question: what does the full zoom from hair to DNA look like?
beats.visual_answer: nested rings shrinking from hair width to cell to mitochondrion to DNA strand, one continuous dive

beats.narration: Inside that power plant, folded cristae burn your sugar into usable energy, machinery 80 times thinner than the hair it hides under.
beats.claim: a mitochondrion about 1 micrometer wide burns sugar into ATP inside folded cristae membranes
beats.visual_question: what is doing the work down there?
beats.visual_answer: macro detail of one mitochondrion with folded cristae glowing warm in its matrix

beats.narration: Uncoil the DNA in one nucleus and it stretches 2 meters, yet the strand is only 2 nanometers wide, 40,000 times thinner than your hair.
beats.claim: the DNA in one human cell uncoils to about 2 meters, yet the double helix is only 2 nanometers wide
beats.visual_question: how much DNA hides in one nucleus?
beats.visual_answer: a 2-meter DNA thread laid beside a cell, with the 2-nanometer helix magnified at its end

beats.narration: So next time you brush your hair, remember the universe in its shadow: 30 trillion cells, each carrying machines you will never see.
beats.claim: the human body holds roughly 30 trillion cells, each a nested universe of unseen machines
beats.visual_question: what should you see when you look at your own hair now?
beats.visual_answer: the machines doing the work down there — 30 trillion glowing cells beneath a single hair, each one a hidden universe
